content: Dutch standards are environmental pollutant reference values that are utilized in processes such as environmental remediation, investigation, and cleanup. These values are specifically calculated for what is referred to as a Standard Soil, which is defined as soil containing 10% organic matter and 25% lutum (a term derived from the Latin word for mud or clay). For groundwater, the reference values are dependent on the depth at which the sample is taken. The values provided here are applicable to shallow groundwater, which is defined as groundwater located at a depth of 0 to 10 meters. An environmental contamination case is classified as serious if more than 25 cubic meters of soil or more than 100 cubic meters of groundwater are contaminated above the established intervention value.
